title: The heart as a lump of flesh
word: The heart as a lump of flesh
hook: there is a lump of flesh in the body: if it is sound, all is sound. it is the heart (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, ikhlas, sincerity, and your line: intention is everything. Did your good deed go unnoticed, and was that all right? Today, a new part of the path begins. Day one thousand two hundred eighty-one.

Put a hand flat on the left side of your chest. Under it, a muscle is doing its work without being asked. The Prophet ﷺ pointed at something like it in a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, narrated by al-Nu'man ibn Bashir. Truly, in the body there is a lump of flesh. If it is sound, the whole body is sound. If it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Truly, it is the heart. One small piece of the body, and everything else follows it. Today, the part of the path that looks after that piece.
screen: `A HAND ON YOUR CHEST.` → `A LUMP OF FLESH.` → `TRULY, IT IS THE HEART.`

segments.voice: The heart in Arabic is qalb, and in the hadith it's called a mudghah, a small piece of flesh. That's the surprise. The thing everything depends on is small, and plain, and easy to overlook. Muslim teachers read it as pointing through the organ that pumps blood, to the inner center of a person, the place where intentions are made. Yesterday's ikhlas lives there. So does every station from these two weeks. Another hadith, in Sahih Muslim, says Allah does not look at your bodies or your appearance, but looks at your hearts and your deeds. And the Qur'an names what will help on the last day. In Pickthall's translation, it is the day when wealth and sons avail not, "Save him who bringeth unto Allah a whole heart." A whole heart, a sound one, qalb salim. That word sound is the hinge. Hearts can be healthy, and hearts can get sick. This new part of the path takes the sicknesses one at a time: arrogance, envy and others, the way a doctor would. First, though, look back at this week. Gratitude with the whole self. The tied camel. Contentment, even through tears. Love that follows. Fear and hope, two wings. Sincerity. All of it was heart-work. The Prophet ﷺ is reported to have asked Allah, the Turner of hearts, to make his heart firm. Even he asked for his heart to be kept.
screen: `QALB: A SMALL PIECE OF FLESH.` · `ALLAH LOOKS AT YOUR HEARTS.` · `A WHOLE HEART: QALB SALIM.` · `HEARTS CAN GET SICK.`

segments.voice: The practice: place a hand on your heart. Settle, and breathe. Rest your palm flat on your chest and leave it there. Feel the beat, steady, asking nothing from you. Let that be the reminder: this small thing is keeping you alive right now. Then ask the inward question, gently. How is the other heart today, the one the hadith points through? Heavy, light, busy, tight, calm? Just name it in one word. No fixing. If you pray, you can recall the Prophet's words: O Turner of hearts. If not, just keep your hand where it is and breathe. The bell holds the time.
The heart as a lump of flesh. The qalb: a small piece of the body that everything follows; when it is sound, all of you is sound. Today's word.
screen: `THE HEART AS A LUMP OF FLESH — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: if the heart is sound. Today, once, put your hand on your chest before you answer someone, and check how your heart is before you speak. Tomorrow, the disease of arrogance. Day one thousand two hundred eighty-one.

howItsDone: Muslims learn this hadith as a teaching that the heart, the inner center of a person, governs everything else, and teachers of the inward path speak of keeping the heart sound and treating its diseases.

fork.setup: the Prophet ﷺ says there is one piece of flesh in the body that everything else follows. which is it?
fork.reveal: if it is sound, the whole body is sound; if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. truly, it is the heart.

original.note: Arabic: a small piece of flesh, a morsel: the hadith's word for the heart.

trapdoor: what you thought: the heart is where feelings live.
what it means: the heart is the inner center that steers the whole person; if it is sound, all of you is sound.
what a scholar hears: mudghah, a morsel of flesh, in al-Nu'man ibn Bashir's hadith, and qalb salim, the whole heart of 26:89.

sources.quoted: Save him who bringeth unto Allah a whole heart.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 52 (al-Nu'man ibn Bashir: in the body is a lump of flesh)
Sahih Muslim 2564 (Allah looks at your hearts and deeds)
Jami' al-Tirmidhi 2140 (O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm)

notes: Pickthall 26:88–89 ('The day when wealth and sons avail not (any man) / Save him who bringeth unto Allah a whole heart.'): confirm exact wording.
Bukhari 52: the hadith is paraphrased (the halal/haram opening is left out; it is taught on day 1434). Confirm number and paraphrase.
Mudghah glossed as 'a small piece of flesh, the kind of morsel you could chew': confirm the lexical gloss.
Muslim 2564 and Tirmidhi 2140: confirm numbers and paraphrases.
Week end (1275–1281) and start of the part 'The diseases of the heart' (1281–1290): the teach looks back at the week and names the part ahead (arrogance, envy).

Editor: cut the 'morsel you could chew' etymology (claims rule) and the superlative 'the one thing'; the reading of the heart as the inner center is now attributed to Muslim teachers rather than stated as the hadith's meaning.
